- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5510, 8682, 9061, 9380, 10151, 10535, 10721, 12360 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: Some reissue paths reset `stall_recovery_count` but omit `phase_attempts = {}`, so replacement issues inherit an exhausted phase-attempt map and can immediately skip recovery.
  WHY: moonshot calls this critical and minimax reports the same omission in two reissue sites; severity disagreement is critical vs high.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1077-1099, 1084-1087, 1120-1123 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `MAX_BUDGET_NEUTRAL_OVERRIDES` and `MAX_JUDGE_REPLAY` accept digits-only input but are not canonicalized to base 10, so leading-zero values can trip bash arithmetic.
  WHY: Deepseek, moonshot, and qwen all identify the missing `10#` normalization on the validation block; leading-zero values can later fail bash arithmetic with "value too great for base".
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6513, 6515 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: `MAX_JUDGE_REPLAY` is interpolated in arithmetic expansion without base-10 canonicalization, so leading-zero values can crash the shell at the replay counter formatting site.
  WHY: Z-ai points to the downstream arithmetic expansion site where `MAX_JUDGE_REPLAY` is used directly, which is the same leading-zero/octal failure mode.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6587-6596 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The cache-write comment still says "Cache the EFFECTIVE action" even though the code caches `_judge_executed_action`, so the documentation no longer matches the implementation.
  WHY: All four reviewers agree the code is correct but the comment is stale, so this is documentation-only.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3334-3340 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The `_list_integration_conflict_files` docstring describes the merge direction opposite to the `git merge-tree` invocation.
  WHY: Moonshot notes the comment claims default-into-integration while the command computes the reverse direction, which can confuse maintainers.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:117-123 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: `test_detect_editor_changes_lost.py` appears to run twice in the "Orchestrator unit tests" step.
  WHY: The duplicate command adds no value and wastes CI time.
- .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:214-220 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: Same duplication of `test_detect_editor_changes_lost.py` as in ci.yml.
  WHY: The duplicate command adds no value and wastes CI time in release workflows.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1084-1087 (MAX_BUDGET_NEUTRAL_OVERRIDES), 1120-1123 (MAX_JUDGE_REPLAY) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Both variables validate with `^[0-9]+$` but are never canonicalized with `$(( 10#${VAL} ))`, so leading-zero values can trip bash arithmetic.
  WHY: A setting like `08` passes validation and then can fail in downstream `-ge` comparisons with "value too great for base".
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:6593-6595 (comment block) | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The cache-write preamble says "Cache the EFFECTIVE action..." but the code caches `_judge_executed_action`, so the comment is stale and truncated.
  WHY: The code path is correct, but the misleading comment can confuse maintainers about whether fallback dispatch results are cached.
